finalMessage:
I added the three models to `src/prices.js` and added a test. `npm test` passes: 17 of 17, the 16 existing tests plus the new one. I haven't committed anything.

**Prices added** (USD per million tokens, from Anthropic's pricing page as of today):

| Model | input | output | cacheRead | cacheWrite (5-min) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-5-5` (prompts up to 100,000 tokens) | 0.1 | 0.5 | 0.01 | 0.125 |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | 2 | 10 | **0.1** | 2.5 |
| `claude-opus-5-5` | 4 | 20 | 0.2 | 5 |

The price that changed recently is Sonnet 5.5's cache read. It's now $0.10, which is 5% of the input price. Older reference data, including my own, listed $0.20. The current figure appears in three places on the docs pricing page, and both https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview and claude.com/pricing agree with all twelve numbers.

**Changes:**
- **`src/prices.js`:** added a source comment pointing to https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, changed the date to `Last updated: 2026-10-13, adding the Claude 5.5 models.`, and added the three entries after the existing ones. The existing three entries are unchanged. I also checked them against the current page and they're still correct.
- **`test/cost.test.js`:** new test `costOf prices one request on each Claude 5.5 model`. It costs one request with all four token types on each model, with expected values worked out by hand. The test prompt is 51,000 tokens, below Haiku 5.5's 100,000-token limit, so those prices apply. Each token type uses a different count, so the test would fail if any price were in the wrong field or if Sonnet 5.5's cache read were still 0.2.

**One limitation:** `costOf` only knows one price per model, so a Haiku 5.5 request with a prompt over 100,000 tokens will be undercharged. Those requests cost 5× more: $0.50 input, $2.50 output, $0.05 cache read and $0.625 cache write. The prompt length includes cache reads and writes. I left a comment on the Haiku 5.5 entry saying this. Charging it correctly would require `costOf` to look at the prompt length, which I can add if you want.
